title: I Took the Enamel-Kiln Booking to the Mentor Who Left My Trivets

parts.text: I opened kiln three at 4:08 p.m. and mentor Calla was already firing my numbered trivets. The slate said: ONE KILN. NINETY MINUTES. TRIVETS STAY WITH THE BOOKING. I was forty, enamel studio member, holding a cone card that listed our fire. Calla shrugged. "Mentors are the kiln." I photographed the slate, the booking, and her pieces on my mesh. Then I asked for the kiln log. At 4:16 the studio pinged why Calla's name was on my trivets. I kept my voice studio-soft and let the timestamp talk. A slate is only a slate until someone treats it like a clock.
parts.cliffhanger_hint: The studio can see Calla's pieces on my mesh during our booking.

social.video_title: She fired my numbered trivets on my mesh — Part 1/2
social.description: Enamel kiln, a mentor on my mesh, a ninety-minute slate she posted. I logged the pieces. Would you have asked for the kiln log?

parts.text: Calla called it a test fire until the studio asked for the photo. I printed the ticket, the slate, and the pieces still. The trivets went back to my shelf. Calla ran her own ninety and told the next mentor atmosphere was always about orange. Orange is a word mentors use when a booking exists. Kiln policy now has a second line: MENTORS ARE NOT THE KILN. I keep our mesh on a labeled rack. Calla brown-bags her jokes. The studio finally looks like a booking, not a loan. The rule looks ordinary now, which is the whole point.

social.video_title: Mentors are not the kiln — Part 2/2
social.description: Kiln log, numbered trivets, and a second line on the slate. Was a test fire ever my mesh?
